0.0.n: This time word sets when the visit happened.

0.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic, setting the time frame for the sentence.

0.2.n: Goes directly before a noun to point out something near the speaker.

0.3.n: Refers to the event the speaker came to view.

0.4.n: Marks 展覧会 as what the speaker wants to see.

0.5.n: The stem of 見る, used before に to express the purpose of coming.

0.6.n: After a verb stem, に marks the purpose of movement.

0.7.n: The polite past form of 来る; the speaker has arrived at the exhibition.

1.0.n: This is the family name; Japanese names usually put the family name first.

1.1.n: This is the given name of the designer 森英恵.

1.2.n: Added after her full name to show everyday respect.

1.3.n: Marks 森英恵さん as the person the sentence is about.

1.4.n: The country name, linked to her occupation by の.

1.5.n: Links Japan to her occupation, describing her as a Japanese designer.

1.6.n: An English-derived job title written in katakana.

1.7.n: A polite ending identifying her occupation.

2.0.n: Describes appearance here, rather than cleanliness, which is another common sense.

2.1.n: Connects きれい to the following noun so it can describe it.

2.2.n: An English-derived word in katakana; Japanese nouns do not require plural endings.

2.3.n: Lists examples rather than giving a complete list.

2.4.n: A general term for clothing, listed alongside ドレス.

2.5.n: Marks ドレスや服 as the things she designed.

2.6.n: The て-form of デザインする connects designing to the following action; the final verb supplies past tense.

2.7.n: 中 adds the sense of covering the whole world.

2.8.n: Links 世界中 to 人, describing where the people are.

2.9.n: Refers collectively to people worldwide; Japanese does not require a plural ending here.

2.10.n: Marks the people who received her message.

2.11.n: The country name modifies ファッション through の.

2.12.n: Links 日本 to ファッション, making the phrase Japanese fashion.

2.13.n: An English-derived noun written in katakana.

2.14.n: Links ファッション to すばらしさ, identifying what has this wonderful quality.

2.15.n: Adding さ to すばらしい turns the describing word into a noun naming its quality.

2.16.n: Marks 日本のファッションのすばらしさ as what she conveyed.

2.17.n: The polite past form of 伝える, used for communicating something to others.

0.lit: Today, as for, this exhibition to see came.
0.tip: A verb stem plus に来ました means came to do that action.

1.lit: Mori Hanae, respectful suffix, as for, Japan's fashion designer is.
1.tip: 日本の before an occupation describes someone as Japanese.

2.lit: Beautiful dresses and clothes designed, and to people worldwide Japanese fashion's wonderfulness conveyed.
2.tip: The て-form connects the two actions, while the final ました makes the sentence polite and past.
